links.reason: Devanthi's பழம்பிறப்பில் ... நோன்பு பொய்த்தாய் (56) explains Kannaki's present lack of her husband, while the goddess's சாபம் பட்டனிர் (169-170) explains the killing; two former-birth causes for different things are not incompatible claims. The poem never answers Devanthi, so 'left standing as a mistaken reading' is the linker's inference, not the text's.

314 (இன்னாசெய் தாரை ஒறுத்தல் ... நன்னயஞ் செய்து விடல்) governs a person's response to injury, 550 (வேந்தொறுத்தல்) the king's to murderers; that is different advice for different situations, which the brief says is no tension. 'The word keeps its form while the ethics divide' only restates the shared word ஒறுத்தல்.

The line is a real quotation: வளம்தலை மயங்கிய நனந்தலை மறுகும் (21) is Pattinappaalai 193 word for word, and 18-19 also borrow its goods (ஆரமும் அகிலும், முத்தும் மணியும் பொன்னும், துகிர்). Since the epic still attaches the line to a list of goods (16-20), 'moves from what flows into the port to who works in it' misdescribes where it falls, and the Pattinappaalai elsewhere shows the port's people, so 'whom its own poem leaves out' is overstated.

Neelakesi's refrain துக்கம் துக்கம் ... சருவம் துக்கம் is a parody of 'all is suffering', and the Manimekalai teacher gives the cause துன்பம் தோற்றம் பற்றே காரணம் (186), so the point that the parody drops the cause is fair. But the Manimekalai unit never states 'all is suffering', so the two do not oppose each other on one claim. It reads better as a refuted view set beside its own school's version than as a tension.
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 256 line 2 (மானறா நோக்கி மணற்சுமை) is unclear.

links.reason: Both use the same charter: Silappathikaram 6:20-24 (ஆயிரம் கண்ணோன் ... உருப்பசி ... சாபம் பெற்ற மங்கை மாதவி வழிமுதல்) and Chithirapathi's count at 24:9-15 (ஆயிரம்கண்ணோன் அவிநயம் வழூஉக்கொள ..., உருப்பசி முனிந்த என் குலத்து ஒருத்தியும்). In one it certifies Madhavi's art, and in the other Chithirapathi measures her shame by it (யான் உறு துன்பம் யாவரும் பட்டிலர், 17) when Madhavi takes the bowl. That reversal is specific.
links.text_issue: Who exactly was cursed in Silappathikaram 6:20-24 is syntactically unsettled.

links.reason: Neelakesi 780 takes the opponent's துய்த்தலும் காண்டலும் to grant knowledge to every soul, and Manimekalai's Sankhya speaker calls purusha ஒன்றாய் எங்கும் பரந்து ... உணர்வாய் (231-232). The Jain answer is aimed at the Sankhya view, and the Manimekalai only records that view, so the pair is a doctrine and its rebuttal across books, not two works in tension. The Manimekalai unit also never speaks of enjoying.

The pairing works as an extension: Neelakesi charges the sacrificers with the killing (கொலைகளும் இரங்கலிர் ... அருவினை யாநுமக்கே), and the Kural sets one abstention above a thousand rites. But the Kural's rite is அவிசொரிந்து, an oblation of ghee, and its abstention is உயிர்செகுத்து உண்ணாமை, not killing and eating. So the gain 'the oblations it sets aside are themselves animal killing' reads the Neelakesi into the couplet.

Both hold that the self is other than the body (உடம்பொடு வேறெனும் ஓர்ப்பு; துச்சில் இருந்த உயிர்), but that is the whole of the connection. Kural 340 is a rhetorical question implying the soul has no lasting home in the body, not a doubt, so 'doubtful question' and 'gains an answer' misdescribe it.

The contrast is real: Manimekalai 29:381-384 sets out the failed example for both 'ஆகாசம் அசத்து' and 'உண்டு' without choosing, while Neelakesi fixes the denial on the Buddhist (அலகில்லாப் பெரும்பரப்பின் ஆகாயம் நினக்கில்லை). But the Manimekalai passage is a technical fallacy example, not a statement about space, so the pair is thin.

Kovalan's விடுதல் அறியா விருப்பினன் (174) and Aravanar's பற்றின் வருவது முன்னது (66) do meet, and Madhavi brings Aravanar காதலன் உற்ற கடுந் துயர் (63). But the teaching is the general cause of the suffering of the born, and nothing in it diagnoses the garland scene. The link is a shared theme of attachment that takes a generous reading to make more.
links.text_issue: The Manimekalai end is a span over units 2:42-57 and 2:58-75.

links.reason: Kundalakesi 1 praises a lord who பிறர்க்கே உறுதிக்கு உழந்தான், and Neelakesi 222 mocks a monkey lying with its tail out, unaware that limbs are for rising against killers. The Buddhist praise and the Jain mockery of self-offering do conflict. But the Neelakesi verse says nothing of the gift profiting no one, and the invocation names no bodily self-offering, so 'intention versus result' is the linker's frame.
links.text_issue: The sense of Neelakesi 222 is flagged uncertain, and Kundalakesi is a fragment.

links.reason: Kural 331 warns against நில்லாத வற்றை நிலையின என்றுணரும் புல்லறிவு, a moral error about wealth and life. Mokkalan's dilemma (நிலையுதல் ... நாசத்தவமெனில் ... நவநவமாம்) is an ontological argument about whether a thing can act if it lasts. The pairing rests on the shared idea of lasting, and the couplet assumes no metaphysical division.
links.text_issue: The detail of Neelakesi 377 line 2 is unclear.

links.reason: Maadalan's law (நற்றிறம் புரிந்தோர் பொற்படி எய்தலும் ... அறப்பயன் விளைதலும் மறப்பயன் விளைதலும், 136-139) does fill out the patikam's ஊழ்வினை உருத்துவந்து ஊட்டும் (57), so develops fits. But the unit tells of one herdswoman, Madari, reborn as Sedakkudumbi's daughter through காதல் (132-135), not of 'the mothers' reborn beside the pathini, and the law is in a Brahmin's mouth.

Neelakesi refutes பையச் சொல்லுதல் நல்வினை by the soft-spoken plotter, and Kural 91 makes sweet speech ஈரம் அளைஇப் படிறுஇலவாம். Its no-deceit clause excludes exactly that case. The pair teaches something specific: the rule she attacks is the Kural's with its guard removed.

Kural 264 says ஒன்னார்த் தெறலும் ... எண்ணின் தவத்தான் வரும். Neelakesi 49 says only that the sage would make her see her powerlessness (இவள் திறமின்மை) and come to the dharma, and it never mentions a power to destroy that he holds back. The restraint the link reads into the verse is supplied by the link.

The two texts conflict on a defensible reading. Manimekalai 30:40 (யானும் இன்றி என்னதும் இன்றி) denies an I in the chain, while Neelakesi argues that whatever carries the traces across moments is a soul, like the thread in a garland (பெருந்தாமத்து உண்ணூல்போல் ... உயிர்). The teaches is accurate that the Manimekalai also grants continuity (பின்போக்கு அல்லது பொன்றக் கெடாதாய், 38) and that the quarrel is over a thread.

Both verses do attack சருவம் துக்கம், one as a monk's grumble and one (இறுதி இஃது துன்பமே இன்பம் இல் ஆயினால் ... தீப்புகாய்) as removing any reason for conduct. But 556 draws its consequence from the doctrine, not from 256, so 'develops' only records that the poet makes the same attack twice.

Kovalan's சலம்புணர் கொள்கைச் சலதியொடு ஆடி ... இலம்பாடு நாணுத் தரும் (69-71) is the couplet's judgment that இருமனப் பெண்டிர் are the company of திருநீக்கப் பட்டார். The narrator then gives his journey another author, வினைகடைக் கூட்ட (78). The pair shows the maxim held as a ruined man's self-account, and the cause the story names is a limit the couplet does not foresee.

There is a real contrast: Ainkurunuru 245's பொய்யா மரபின் ஊர் முது வேலன் gets the cause wrong, while Saalini, a possessed மூதறி வாட்டி, names Kannaki divine and Kannaki calls it பேதுறவு. But the velan is diagnosing love-sickness and Saalini is giving praise in possession, so the reversal of 'the Sangam irony' needs a generous reading. The epic gain, that Kannaki's dismissal is a known akam stance, is not in the Tamil.

Both poems concern Evvi's death in battle: Purananuru 233 wishes the report of எவ்வி மார்பின் எஃகுஉறு விழுப்புண் பல false, and Akananuru 115 recalls எவ்வி வீழ்ந்த செருவில் பாணர் and their lute necks. The broken lute is only in the Akam poem, so there is no shared image. The pair is a death denied and a death remembered.

The goddess's அவ் அறம் நின்னாங்கு ஒழியாது (10:40-41) is answered by Manimekalai's ஆங்கு அதன் பயனே ஆர் உயிர் மருந்து ஆய் ஈங்கு இப் பாத்திரம் என் கைப் புகுந்தது (11:105-106). That is a prophecy and its fulfilment, and the note says so. The teaches holds: the fruit comes first as a means of further giving, under Deepathilakai's condition (அருள் சுரந்து ஊட்டும் சிறந்தோர்க்கு அல்லது ... சுரவாது).

Both use the same image. Kundalakesi 14's body where நுனைய புழுக்குலம் ... நுகரவும் வாழவும் பட்ட shows it is not 'I' or 'mine', and Neelakesi's உடம்பினுள்ள பல்லுயிர் சாவ makes the bodhisattva's gift of his body many killings. The same teeming body serves non-self on one side and non-harm on the other, which neither verse shows alone.

Naladiyar 38's small seed and தக்கார்கைப் பட்டக்கால் growth meet the goddess's gift that ஒழியாது நின் பிறப்பு அறுத்திடும் (41) and her seed image of Lakshmi as அறத்தின் வித்து that might fall on வெந்து உகு வெங் களர் (46-48). The epic raises the harvest to the end of births and puts a condition on the giver that the quatrain does not state. Both gains hold.

The Kural's ஐயம் is the spiritual doubt that keeps the sky far. Manimekalai's சங்கயம் (274) names a technical fallacy, a reason that admits a contrary reason in a debate about whether sound is eternal. The pair joins two senses of 'doubt', and neither text says that clarity cannot come from matching proofs.

This is an order and its fulfilment. Kannaki bids the fire spare பார்ப்பார் அறவோர் பசு ... and go to the தீத்திறத்தார் (21:53-55), and the fire spares the virtuous (அறவோர் மருங்கின் அழற்கொடி விடாது) and the cows and calves (கறவையும் கன்றும் கனலெரி சேரா) while the warriors' quarter burns (22:113-116). The அறவோர்/மறவோர் pun carries the teaches.
links.text_issue: In 22:113 விடாது could be read the other way. Line 111 is doubted in the edition, and kaathai 22 has lines marked as later additions.

links.reason: Kural 355 asks one to see the மெய்ப்பொருள் whatever a thing's nature. Neelakesi 499 argues that nothing is made known except through its qualities (குணமுகத்தால் அன்றி), against a Buddhist demand to be shown the soul. Turning the couplet's 'whatever its nature' into a Jain method stretches a general maxim to fit a technical point, and the couplet leaves no question open.

Silappathikaram 5:65-66 already says why the bhuta came: வெற்றிவேல் மன்னற்கு உற்றதை ஒழிக்க எனத் தேவர் கோமான் ஏவலின் போந்த. Kaathai 6 adds only the asura war and the five halls, so the claim that the city's rite does not explain itself is false. What remains is a fuller retelling in sequence.

The verses do not make the same claim: Thirikadugam faults song கொட்டி அளந்தமையா (not measured to the beat), and Innaa Narpathu faults singing to a யாழ் that is பண்ணமையா (not set to its mode). They complement each other, and two stock items of painful things are a thin pairing.
links.text_issue: The sense of Thirikadugam 57 lines 2-3 is uncertain.

links.reason: Neelakesi's list உழப்பு அறிவு குறி செய்கை does not match Manimekalai's நுகர்ச்சி குறிப்பே பாவனை உள்ள அறிவு term for term, so 'accepts the list term for term' is false. The Manimekalai unit names the five aggregates but does not here deny them an owner, so the tension depends on doctrine outside the unit.

The goddess's saying that ஆடித் திங்கள் ... ஒள்ளெரி உண்ண உரைசால் மதுரையோடு அரைசு கேடுறும் (23:133-136) explains the fire god's பண்டேயோர் ஏவல் உடையேன் (21:51-52). The later unit gives the earlier one's standing order a foretold date, and the teaches is accurate that Kannaki's act is the trigger of a fixed sentence.

The patikam's ஊழ்வினை உருத்துவந்து ஊட்டும் and Tirumanthiram's சிவனருளால் வினை சேரகிலாமை differ on whether a deed must be eaten. But the Tirumanthiram's grace is an exception that presupposes deeds otherwise cling, and the patikam says nothing about release either way. The claim that the epic offers no intervening grace goes beyond these lines.

The venba's மாமகள் நாமகள் ... மாமயிடற் செற்றுகந்த கோமகள் is pictured in the next kaathai as a goddess with a lotus in one hand and a sword in the other, a கழல் on one foot and a சிலம்பு on the other. This is description in story order. Saraswati has no part in the picture, and the divided body (also சடையும் பிறையும்) is not built only from the venba's three goddesses.

The mantra given at 10:80-82 (வேற்று உரு எய்தவும் அந்தரம் திரியவும்) is used at 23:52-53 (நா இயல் மந்திரம் ... ஆண்மைக் கோலத்து), so it is a gift fulfilled. But the goddess gives it because no one would tell a young girl விளை பொருள், that is, to hear the schools, not as a defence against slander. The Manimekalai has also changed form before this, so 'first used' is false.

Aravanar's deferral (ஆங்கு அவை நிகழ்ந்த பின்னர் அல்லது ... பொருளுரை பொருந்தாய், 12:106-107) is answered when Manimekalai, having rejected the five schools, asks அடிகள் மெய்ப்பொருள் அருளுக (29:45). The note says which.

Both poems close on the left-eye omen (உண் கண்ணும் ஆடுமால் இடனே; கண் ஆடும் இடம்). This is a shared stock sign, not one poem developing the other. The observation that it can carry a whole venba is fair but thin.

Mokkalan's கன்று முயலுங் கழுதை ... கோடு ... எழலில்லை and the Manimekalai's முயற்கோடு இன்மையின் தோற்றமும் இல் (216) use the same example for a non-thing, so agrees fits. But the hare's horn is the stock non-existent of every school, so the pairing shows little beyond the shared example.
links.text_issue: Why கன்று appears in Neelakesi 404 line 1 is unclear.

links.reason: Naladiyar 121 makes the meat-eater's belly a burning ground (புல்லறிவாளர் வயிறு) as a metaphor. Neelakesi 32 describes a literal சுடலை with flesh-eating demons around the shrine of the கூளி தாய், with no word on eating flesh as a fault. The link rests on the shared word 'burning ground'.

Neelakesi 587 turns the opponent's own account (தீயுழப்பே செயும் தீவினை) on the Buddha: நீயுழப்பாய் பிறர்க்கே உழந்தாயால். That is close to Kural 320's நோயெல்லாம் நோய்செய்தார் மேலவாம, and the hard case of the helper is a real limit. But the verse applies the Buddhist definition, not the Kural's rule as the note says, and whose pain is meant is unsettled.

The epic's அல்லலுற் றாற்றா தழுவாளை (19:15) is close to the couplet's அல்லற்பட்டு ஆற்றாது அழுத, and the note claims a shared condition, not a quotation. The citizens at once read the tears as வளையாத செங்கோல் வளைந்தது (18). One woman's tears become the verdict on the king that the couplet states as a slow wearing, and both gains hold.

The goddess's மறைநா ஓசை அல்லது யாவதும் மணிநா ஓசை கேட்டதும் இலனே (23:31-32) answers Kannaki's Chola precedent of வாயிற் கடைமணி நடுநா நடுங்க (20:63). The later unit answers the earlier, and the note names the answer.

The ancestor learns of the wrong by inquiry (கொடுங்கோல் உண்டுகொல் ... அறிந்தீமின், 111-112), owns it (என் இறைமுறை பிழைத்தது) and repairs it with land. Nedunjeliyan, the தேரா மன்னன், owns his only after the gem flies (யானே கள்வன், 85) and pays with his life. The counter-case qualifies the king's fault by when he inquires.

The two give incompatible accounts of who acts in release. The epic says the disciple, under a great one who only gives dharma (பிறர்க்கு அறம் அருளும் பெரியோன்), is saved by cutting dependence himself (சார்பு அறுத்து உய்தி, 179). Tirumanthiram 1527 has grace come as the guru (இன்னருட் சத்தி குருவென வந்து) and release follow when one's own agency ends (தன்செயல் அற்றால்). This is the grace-versus-own-effort tension the round tests.

Neelakesi's regress (தன்னைப் படைப்பின் ... முடிவில்லை) attacks a maker, and Kural 1's ஆதி பகவன் முதற்றே உலகு makes the Lord first but says nothing of making. The teaches itself concludes that the argument leaves the couplet standing, so the two are not in tension: the debate limits what the couplet can be taken to claim.
